name: What information should I have ready before getting a room-addition consultation?

mainEntity.name: What information should I have ready before getting a room-addition consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Before contacting a room-addition company, collect the property address, approximate room dimensions, photos, a rough sketch, desired use, preferred location, and any known plans or permits. Also note household priorities such as accessibility, bathroom needs, storage, outdoor-space preservation, and construction timing.

Context: Information about the existing home helps the team identify whether the project is a footprint addition, garage conversion, second-story concept, or broader reconfiguration. Photos of the roof, foundation, electrical panel, yard, and access route can reveal questions early.

Key factors:
- Existing surveys, plans, inspection reports, and permits
- Property constraints and known easements
- Budget range and must-have features
- Material, style, and timing preferences

Practical guidance: Create a one-page project brief and list questions about permits, design fees, allowances, schedule, insurance, supervision, and change orders. Be candid about prior leaks, unpermitted work, or contractor experiences.

Elite Remodeling & Design can use that information to shape an initial consultation around the homeowner’s intended use and property conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Prepare the address, photos, rough dimensions, desired room use, preferred location, budget range, timing, and any plans, permits, surveys, or inspection reports. Also list must-have features, accessibility needs, storage goals, and known problems such as leaks or prior unpermitted work.
